then.text: I'm off to the Bodleian to apologise in person. Possibly in writing, possibly in verse.
A bestiary leaf? I? What a suggestion. I'm merely, ah, reading a leaf. By a fire. In the pub where the Inklings met. It's atmospheric. It's research!
Oh, take it. It's been a joy and a worry. I've sworn the Declaration three times and this is the first time I've broken it. Not the fire, I haven't lit it. The fireplace is somebody else's.
Tell the Librarian I'll write. In Latin, so it won't be read.

else.text: Welcome to the Eagle and Child. Do sit down, and don't mind me. I'm reading. Nothing important. A leaf, of the... ah. Of the news. Of the day.

ox_landlord.text: The Eagle and Child, known as the Bird and Baby. It's the pub where the Inklings met, the writers' group, in the back room from the 1930s to 1962.
Tolkien and Lewis read chapters aloud on Tuesday lunchtimes and criticised them with great enthusiasm. A great many of the arguments about whether they were any good happened right here.

ox_inkling.text: I'm writing a book in the back room. Not really, but it's polite to look as though you might be.
The Inklings read their work aloud and everyone was rude about it. It's called constructive criticism. The 'constructive' bit is optional.

ox_quizmaster.text: Quiz night at the Eagle and Child! Five questions, no phones, and nobody quoting Tolkien at me. I've had enough of hobbits for one night.
Fancy a round? Five questions, no phones.

else.text: Suit yourself. The crisps are salt and vinegar either way.
